How the stack is wired and every setting that matters, with pointers to the repo that owns each one.

> **Where to run this.** Docker Compose commands run inside a clone of this repository (`git clone https://github.com/grand-stack/grandstack`, then `cd grandstack`), with the repositories it builds cloned beside it. The [quickstart](/docs/grandstack/#quickstart) has the exact steps.

## Compose services

`compose.yaml` defines three services:

| Service | Image or build | Ports (host:container) | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `neo4j` | `neo4j:2026.10-community` | 7474:7474 (browser), 7687:7687 (bolt) | Data in the named volume `neo4j-data`. Healthcheck runs `cypher-shell`; the server waits for it. |
| `server` | built from `../grandstack-server` | 4000:4000 | Needs Neo4j healthy first. |
| `web` | built from `../grandstack-web` | 3000:8080 | Static files served by unprivileged nginx. |

Because the builds use `../grandstack-server` and `../grandstack-web`, **the three repositories must sit side by side in one folder.** The auth setup also builds from `../grandstack-auth`, the agents setup from `../grandstack-agents`, and the federation setup from `../grandstack-federation`, so those repositories must be there too if you use them.

### With authentication: `compose.auth.yaml`

An override file, used together with `compose.yaml`: `docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.auth.yaml up --build`. Development only. It changes and adds:

| Service | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `keycloak` (new) | `quay.io/keycloak/keycloak:26.8.1` in dev mode, imports `../grandstack-auth/keycloak/grandstack-realm.json`, issuer fixed to `http://localhost:8081/realms/grandstack`, port 8081, healthcheck |
| `gateway` (new) | built from `../grandstack-auth/gateway`, in front of the server, port 4000 |
| `auth-client` (new) | the demo client, built from `../grandstack-auth/client`, port 3001 |
| `server` | **no host port**; gets `AUTH_JWKS_URL`, `AUTH_ISSUER`, `AUTH_AUDIENCE`, `SCHEMA_EXTRA_PATHS`, `SETUP_CYPHER_PATHS`; mounts `auth.graphql` and `auth-setup.cypher`; a healthcheck; waits for Keycloak |
| `web` | unchanged: still http://localhost:3000, still calling `http://localhost:4000/graphql`, which is now the gateway, so it is an anonymous client |

Ports in the auth setup: 3000 web, 3001 demo client, 4000 gateway, 8081 Keycloak, 7474 and 7687 Neo4j. Everything else about the auth settings (roles, permissions, rules, the issuer-versus-keys addresses) is documented in `grandstack-auth` (`docs/how-it-works.md`, `docs/role-and-scope-model.md`).

### With agents: `compose.agents.yaml`

An override file, used together with `compose.yaml`: `docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.agents.yaml up --build`. It adds one service:

| Service | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| `agents-mcp` (new) | built from `../grandstack-agents`; MCP over streamable HTTP at `http://localhost:4100/mcp`; `GRAPHQL_URL=http://server:4000/graphql`; `ALLOW_MUTATIONS` from `AGENTS_ALLOW_MUTATIONS` (default `false`) |

It talks to the open server, so it needs the default stack and has no auth of its own. Keep port 4100 on your machine. To use it with the auth setup, give it a token as described in `grandstack-agents` (`docs/adding-auth.md`).

### With federation: `compose.federation.yaml`

An override file, used together with `compose.yaml`: `docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.federation.yaml up --build`. It changes and adds:

| Service | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| `server` | `FEDERATION=true`; mounts `../grandstack-federation/schema/federation.graphql` (`SCHEMA_EXTRA_PATHS`) and `seed/wikipedia-links.cypher` (`SETUP_CYPHER_PATHS`); **host port 4001** instead of 4000; a healthcheck |
| `wikipedia` (new) | built from `../grandstack-federation`; the Wikipedia subgraph, port 4010 |
| `gateway` (new) | built from `../grandstack-federation/gateway`; serves the composed supergraph on **port 4000**; waits for the server and the Wikipedia subgraph |
| `web` | unchanged: still http://localhost:3000, still calling `http://localhost:4000/graphql`, which is now the gateway |

It needs internet for the Wikipedia part, and it replaces the default, auth and agents setups on port 4000. Ports in the federation setup: 3000 web, 4000 gateway, 4001 Neo4j subgraph, 4010 Wikipedia subgraph, 7474 and 7687 Neo4j.

### With Aura management: `compose.aura.yaml`

An override file, used together with `compose.yaml`: `docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.aura.yaml up --build`. It talks to the **real Aura API** by default. It needs `SECRET_KEY` in `.env` (`../grandstack-web-aura/scripts/init-env.sh` makes it). It changes and adds:

| Service | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| `neo4j` | its own volume (`neo4j-aura-data`), ports on `127.0.0.1` only, and a second network `store` |
| `server` | `MODEL=aura` (mounts `../grandstack-web-aura/models`), `READ_ONLY=true`, `FEDERATION=true`; host port 4001; starts after `store-writer` |
| `store-writer` (new) | the same image and model, writable, on the private `store` network only, no published port |
| `aura` (new) | built from `../grandstack-web-aura`; the Aura subgraph, port 4010; needs `SECRET_KEY`; `AURA_BASE_URL` defaults to `https://api.neo4j.io` |
| `gateway` (new) | built from `../grandstack-federation/gateway`, with `../grandstack-web-aura/gateway/supergraph.graphql` and `gateway.config.ts` mounted over its own; port 4000 |
| `web` | built from `../grandstack-web-aura`, **replacing the Movies app**; http://localhost:3000; it forwards `/graphql` to the gateway |

Everything is bound to `127.0.0.1`, because the app can delete databases and has no sign-in. It replaces the default, auth, agents and federation setups on ports 3000 and 4000. `compose.aura-edge.yaml` adds a TLS and sign-in edge on port 8443 and removes every other published port. Ports in the Aura setup: 3000 web, 4000 gateway, 4001 read-only server, 4010 Aura subgraph, 4020 fake Aura, 7474 and 7687 Neo4j.

For development and tests add **`compose.aura-mock.yaml`**: it starts `mock-aura` (built from `../grandstack-web-aura`, a fake Aura API on port 4020, published on this machine only), makes `aura` wait for it, and sets `AURA_BASE_URL` to the fake and `ALLOW_INSECURE_AURA_URL=true`. The address is fixed, not read from `.env`, so a real `AURA_BASE_URL` there cannot send a test to the real Aura. Connect to it with `mock-client` and `mock-secret`.

**Do not run `docker compose down -v` with the default project name to reset the Aura setup beside a Movies stack you want to keep:** the merged files include the Movies data volume as well as the Aura one, and `-v` removes both. Use `-p aura` for the Aura setup.

## Settings you are likely to change

| Setting | Where | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `NEO4J_PASSWORD` | `.env` (copy from `.env.example`) | `grandstack-dev` | Neo4j password; used by Neo4j, the healthcheck and the server. Set before the first start: Neo4j stores the password in the volume. |
| Server variables (`SEED`, `SEED_PATH`, `SEED_PROBE_LABEL`, `REFRESH_COUNTS`, `CORS_ORIGIN`, `NEO4J_DATABASE`, `AUTH_*`, `SCHEMA_EXTRA_PATHS`, `SETUP_CYPHER_PATHS`, ...) | `server.environment` in `compose.yaml` | see the server's `docs/configuration.md` | How the server behaves. Add the ones you need under `server.environment`. |
| `VITE_GRAPHQL_URL` | `web.build.args` in `compose.yaml` | `http://localhost:4000/graphql` | The URL the **browser** uses to reach the server. Fixed at build time, so rebuild `web` after changing it. |
| Host ports | `ports` in `compose.yaml` | 3000, 4000, 7474, 7687 | Change the left side to avoid clashes. If you move the web port, also set the server's `CORS_ORIGIN` to the new web origin. If you move the server port, change `VITE_GRAPHQL_URL`. |

The server's own variable list lives in `docs/configuration.md` in `grandstack-server`; it is the source of truth.

## Everyday commands

```sh
docker compose up --build        # start everything (first run builds the images)
docker compose up -d             # start in the background
docker compose logs -f server    # follow one service
docker compose down              # stop, keep the data
docker compose down -v           # stop and DELETE the Neo4j data (the sample reseeds on next start)
```

Use your own schema and data with an override file: [build your own app](/docs/grandstack/build-your-own-app/).

## Podman

On macOS `docker` may actually be Podman. If commands cannot connect, start the VM with `podman machine start` and set `DOCKER_HOST` to the socket it prints. Compose works the same way. The stack in this repo was developed and tested under Podman.

## Resetting data

The default stack has no authentication, and the app can edit and delete everything. (With the auth setup, editing needs a login with the right role.) To get the sample data back, run `docker compose down -v` then `docker compose up` (add the `-f` files you started with). A seed newer than the loaded one reloads by itself on server start; see the server's `docs/seeding.md`.

## If a port is already in use

If you already run Neo4j (or anything else) on one of these ports, compose may fail to bind it, or a client may reach the wrong server: on the machine this was built on, a local Neo4j listened on `127.0.0.1:7687` while the container's forwarded port was bound as well, so `bolt://localhost:7687` could hit either one. The stack itself is unaffected, because the server reaches Neo4j over the compose network (`bolt://neo4j:7687`). To avoid confusion, change the left side of the port mapping in `compose.yaml` (for example `"17687:7687"`) before connecting a tool from your machine, and check what is listening with `lsof -nP -iTCP:7687 -sTCP:LISTEN`.

## Ports at a glance

| URL | What |
| --- | --- |
| http://localhost:3000 | Web app |
| http://localhost:4000/graphql | GraphQL API and GraphiQL |
| http://localhost:4001/graphql | Neo4j subgraph (federation setup only) |
| http://localhost:4010/graphql | Wikipedia subgraph (federation setup only) or Aura subgraph (Aura setup only) |
| http://localhost:4020/v1 | Fake Aura API (Aura setup only) |
| http://localhost:4100/mcp | Agents MCP server (agents setup only; `/healthz` for a check) |
| http://localhost:7474 | Neo4j Browser (user `neo4j`, password from `.env`) |
| http://localhost:3001 | Auth demo client (auth setup only) |
| http://localhost:8081 | Keycloak (auth setup only; admin console `admin` / `admin`) |
| bolt://localhost:7687 | Neo4j Bolt |
